'''Eviatar Nevo''' ({{Langx|he|אביתר נבו}}; born February 2, 1929, in Haifa, [[Mandatory Palestine]]),<ref>[http://errol.oclc.org/laf/n85-389945.html  LC authorities]</ref> is Professor Emeritus, founder and director of the Institute of Evolution at [[University of Haifa]], Israel.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://evolution.haifa.ac.il/index.php/people/223-eviatar-nevo-ph-d |title=Eviatar Nevo, Institute of Evolution, Haifa University |access-date=2014-08-10 |archive-date=2014-08-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140805222723/http://evolution.haifa.ac.il/index.php/people/223-eviatar-nevo-ph-d |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Research==
 
Nevo received a M.Sc and  PhD (1964) from [[Hebrew University]]. His Ph.D thesis was entitled "Population studies of Anurans from the lower Cretaceous of Makhtesh Ramon, Israel".<ref>[https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/18698038  WorldCat item record]</ref> He founded the Institute of Evolution at Haifa in 1973 and researches [[evolutionary biology]], in particular, speciation processes, modifications of highly evolved traits (vision), climatic and geographic effects in sympatric speciation in insects, bacteria, fungi, mammals and crops. He is a proponent of evolutionary models where environmental stressors act positively to shape genetic polymorphisms.

In 1994, he nicknamed [[Mount Carmel]] "Evolution Canyon" and later proposed a model of the same name that acts as a global warming monitor through observing biodiversity. The EC microscale model can be used when there are two opposite slopes with contrasting climatic conditions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Nevo|first=Eviatar|date=1995-11-22|title=Asian, African and European biota meet at 'Evolution Canyon' Israel: local tests of global biodiversity and genetic diversity patterns|journal=Proc. R. Soc. Lond. B|language=en|volume=262|issue=1364|pages=149–155|doi=10.1098/rspb.1995.0189|bibcode=1995RSPSB.262..149N|s2cid=86456267|issn=0962-8452}}</ref> Studies at Mount Carmel of particular impact and interest have involved [[Drosophila]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Michalak|first1=Pawel|last2=Minkov|first2=Irina|last3=Helin|first3=Amanda|last4=Lerman|first4=Daniel N.|last5=Bettencourt|first5=Brian R.|last6=Feder|first6=Martin E.|last7=Korol|first7=Abraham B.|last8=Nevo|first8=Eviatar|date=2001-11-06|title=Genetic evidence for adaptation-driven incipient speciation of Drosophila melanogaster along a microclimatic contrast in "Evolution Canyon," Israel|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=98|issue=23|pages=13195–13200|doi=10.1073/pnas.231478298|issn=0027-8424|pmid=11687637|pmc=60847|bibcode=2001PNAS...9813195M|doi-access=free}}</ref> and wild [[barley]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kalendar|first1=Ruslan|last2=Tanskanen|first2=Jaakko|last3=Immonen|first3=Sirkka|last4=Nevo|first4=Eviatar|last5=Schulman|first5=Alan H.|date=2000-06-06|title=Genome evolution of wild barley (Hordeum spontaneum) by BARE-1 retrotransposon dynamics in response to sharp microclimatic divergence|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=97|issue=12|pages=6603–6607|doi=10.1073/pnas.110587497|issn=0027-8424|pmid=10823912|pmc=18673|doi-access=free}}</ref>

He has published more than 1000 peer-reviewed research articles on a wide array of topics about genetic diversity, evolution in action, and environmental shaping of evolutionary processes.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://evolution.haifa.ac.il/index.php/component/content/article/29 | title=Evolution}}</ref> According to Thomson Reuters, he is among the top highly cited researchers in the world.<ref>[http://highlycited.com/institution/university-of-haifa.html Thomson Highly Cited record E. Nevo, Haifa]</ref>

==Awards and honors==

He is a Foreign Member of the Linnean Society, London (1990) and of the Ukraine Academy of Sciences (1997). He is a Foreign Associate Member in Evolutionary Biology section of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], USA (2000),<ref>[https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/eviatar-nevo-6v26ui/ "Eviatar Nevo", National Academy of Science]</ref> an Honorary Member of the Ukraine Botanical Society (1995), of the American Society of Mammalogists (2002), and the Israel Zoological Society (2007). He received Honorary doctorates from World University (1990) and the [[University of Duisburg-Essen]], Germany.
